status: source-pinned-CI-success; sham controls show timing drift; compiler-speedup-NOT-qualified

method.inputs: same optimized Rust-generated Wasm compiled with baseline/patched Cranelift; exact archived AOT and compiler hashes checked before unsafe Wasmtime deserialization

modes.aa: baseline AOT instance vs a second baseline AOT instance
modes.bb: patched AOT instance vs a second patched AOT instance

method.methodology: ABBA/BAAB within-block balanced elapsed time, checksums validated against independent signed/unsigned Python arithmetic oracle; trap cases checked in Rust harness
method.ratio: median of each mode's 8 paired within-block patched-slot/baseline-slot ratios; values below 1 indicate lower elapsed time for second slot in that particular mode

interpretation: In the new A/B run, all three positive functions have patched/baseline median ratios slightly above 1; this conflicts with earlier single-host timing patterns, preventing a robust speedup claim.

Even when compared A/A or B/B using the SAME AOT bytes in separate module instances, several within-block median ratios depart from 1 by about 2–3% or more. Therefore location, environment and/or call-site timing effects can mimic the scale of candidate changes.
Negative controls with zero emitted byte-count savings also show A/B timing drift, so no causal performance attribution is supported.
Static per-function x86-64 byte savings remain real within their admitted fixture and are not invalidated by inconclusive timing.
assurance: All three modes passed source pin, AOT hash, finite guest-value, trap and raw timing checksum controls in the identified CI.
No paired confidence interval, independent CPU model, hardware counters, or code-address alignment control; no portable performance conclusion.
The compiler transformation is manually developed and not a synthesized instruction sequence.
No general compiler-pass/VeriISLE or x86 flag/ABI/poison proof; mathematical Euclidean proof is separate.
Zero whole AOT module size saving demonstrated; native decoded instruction bytes are not CLIF operation costs.
next: Use stable code-address/layout-controlled microbenchmarks, confirm meaningful workloads, then assess register liveness and wider compiler-pass verification before upstream proposal.
